about: Layout 3b, the build target of ADR-0010 (2026-10-17): the solver's case 3 (PSU flat, exits free) with the field rail shifted to x 40-324 and two upper-left grommets, so every cable group has a duct path. Centres in mm (x front 0 to back 457, y left 0 to right 330); rot 1 = the block's long side runs along y. Score with layout_study.Score('B', place) after setting Exits to 'exits' and renaming the SHIELD-UL net to SHIELD-ULM. Rescored 2026-10-18 (issue #158): FB1 is a 12-way, so the fuse rail (RFB) is 60 mm longer and the 5 V PSU (PS5) moved to the 24 V row against the back ring, with the lower left grommet (LL) moved from x 292 to 390 past the fuse rail's end; the 2026-10-17 layout scored 34892. Rescored 2026-10-21 (issue #202, ADR-0018): the 24 V PSU measures 240 x 126 x 65, not the assumed 215 x 115 x 50, so the box is 13.5 in wide (y 0 to 342.9), the PSU sits against the front ring (x 23), the PSU and R110 centres and the inlet moved 7.4 mm toward the right wall (12.9 wider, less half the PSU's extra 11 mm) and the upper right grommet (UR) 12.9; the 2026-10-18 layout scored 35929 at the 78.6 bay of the 50 mm PSU. Rescored 2026-10-22 (issue #205): the trunk fuse holder F3 (RT18-32, 3-pole, 54 mm) stands first on the 24 V rail, whose front end moves from x 87 to 32, past cable slot 3; K2 and the bars move 3 mm back and the servo PSU (PS6) with them, R24 is 180.1 long, and the PSU's V+ to FB1 now runs through F3 (nets PSU-R24 4 and R24-RFB 4, PSU-RFB gone); the 2026-10-21 layout scored 36368. Rescored 2026-11-12 (issue #220, ADR-0020): the screen's 12 V DC-DC (PS12, a Mean Well DDR-60G-12 on its own 66.5 mm rail) takes the upper deck's free spot between the shield clamp and the back run, behind cable slot 2, with nets RFB-PS12 1, PS12-R24 1 and PS12-LL 2; no other block moved, and the 2026-10-22 layout scored 36839. Rescored 2026-11-23 (issue #244, ADR-0021): the 5 V PSU (PS5) and the servo PSU (PS6) are Mean Well DDR-30G-5 DIN-rail converters, 35 x 90 x 54.5, both in the 24 V row against the back ring (PS6 at x 357, PS5 at 392.5, each rail 41.5 mm with its ground block at its outer end), since at the old servo PSU's spot the converter's 90 mm depth left 5 mm to the 110 VAC compartment for the PSU trunk; PS6 now runs along x like PS12 (rot 0); nets unchanged, and the 2026-11-12 layout scored 38304. Rescored 2026-11-27 (issue #264): an eighth TB6600 (DRVU, the U axis of the mask library elevator) lies on its own 106 mm rail along x in the strip between the motor duct and the right wall, from the front ring, centre (76.8, 297.9), since neither the drivers' row nor the lower deck has room for it; its nets are RFB-DRVU 1 (F2-12), R24-DRVU 1 (0V-P 2), LOGIC-DRVU 4 (step, direction, enable and COM) and DRVU-SHIELD 4, and SHIELD-UL goes from 24 to 28; 0V-S gains a slice for U's COM, so the logic rail is 6.2 mm longer and LOGIC and SSR move about 3.1 and 6.2 mm back; the 2026-11-23 layout scored 38903. Rescored 2026-11-28 (issue #264, ADR-0022 revised): U moved onto the drivers' rail as its eighth TB6600, so DRV is 276 mm long, centre (161.0, 216.5), with nets RFB-DRV 8, R24-DRV 8, LOGIC-DRV 32 and DRV-SHIELD 32, and DRVU is gone; the shield clamp becomes a shield bar (SHIELD, a Siemens EC2GB152 ground bar for the motor cables' drain wires, drawn 216 x 13 x 13 from its package) along x in the strip between the motor duct and the right wall, its back end 2 mm in front of the back run, 14 mm left along the wall, centre (267.3, 299.4), rot 0; cable slot 1 moved to x 300-313, between the drivers' rail and the 12 V DC-DC's, which moved 3 mm back (PS12 at 344.75); the 2026-11-27 layout scored 43292. Expected wire: 46280 conductor-mm at the study's 85.5 bay (hand layout 57478).
